instruction: Explain overfitting in machine learning to a high school student in simple terms.

It happens because the model has been trained on too much information, which means it has learned all the features and patterns from the training data but not enough from the test data.

For example, if you have a dataset with 1000 samples and 5 features, your model might learn the patterns for each feature separately, even though there are only 2 features left. This can lead to an overly complex model that doesn't generalize well to new data.

To avoid overfitting, you need to split your data into training and validation sets. You then train your model on the training set and evaluate its performance on the validation set. If the model performs poorly on the validation set, you may need to adjust the hyperparameters (such as regularization strength) or retrain the model on the entire training set.
